scaling.rule: Froude scaling: each world is measured in its own board length L and its own gravity g. Lengths in L, times in sqrt(L/g), speeds in sqrt(g L), accelerations in g. Pure ratios (roll-away, speed kept) need no conversion.

game.g: measured by dropping the board in the sim (G in src/sim.ts, 20)

scaling.score: |game - target| <= tol scores 100, falling linearly to 0 at 3 * tol

vert360flat.note: slow motion of unknown factor: heights only, no timing

street09889.note: handrail grind is a slow-motion multi-angle replay: rejected for timing

ollieAir.source: ollie1 f32-41 (9 fr, 0.375 s), ollie2 f52-62 (10 fr, 0.417 s), kickflip f77-85.5 (8.5 fr, 0.354 s); mean 0.382 s = 0.18 m pop. +/-1 frame each. Young riders: adult ollies run higher, hence the wide band.

rollAway.unit: speed after landing / speed before pop
rollAway.source: board travel in board lengths per frame, static camera: ollie1 f24-30 vs f45-51 = 0.15 vs 0.155 L/fr (1.03); kickflip f72-76 vs f88-93 (about 1.1, noisy); ollie2 0.69 rejected (rider moving toward camera, foreshortened).

flipTime.source: kickflip f77-82: one full roll of the board in about 5 frames (0.21 s +/- 0.04).

coastDistance.unit: L, coasting from 1.43 sqrt(gL) (4 m/s real) to a stop on flat
coastDistance.source: Kogelbauer, Koyama, Callan, Shinomoto, 'Mechanical Optimization of Skateboard Pumping', arXiv:2312.17671 (Phys. Rev. Research 2024): effective friction mu ~ 0.02 at 3 m/s (dv 0.2 m/s over 1 s). Split as rolling 0.016 g + air 0.004 v^2 per m, integrated from 4 m/s: 43 m = 53 L.

pushTop.source: Crockett & Jensen 2007, 'Kinematic analysis and muscular activity of skateboard propulsion in experienced participants', ISBS proceedings (ojs.ub.uni-konstanz.de/cpa/article/view/555): pushing studied at 8-14 km/h; target a hard push top of 4.5 m/s +/- 1.1.

pushAccel.unit: g, mean from rest to half push top
pushAccel.source: about 0.7 m/s per stroke at about 1 stroke per 0.7 s, consistent with the cadences in Crockett & Jensen 2007. Low weight.

pushGrade.unit: push acceleration up a 6 deg grade plus g sin 6, over the same on flat, from 0.5 sqrt(gL)
pushGrade.source: added by the round-1 judge: a foot reaches the ground on any street grade a rider can stand on, so the push force is the same up a 10% hill as on flat (only gravity is added). Stops PUSH_STEEP-style cut-offs that fix the pipe metrics by disabling pushing on hills.

carveLateral.unit: g, full steer at push top speed
carveLateral.source: a rider leaning about 35 deg into a carve holds tan(35) = 0.7 g; Hubbard, 'Lateral dynamics and stability of the skateboard', J. Appl. Mech. 46 (1979) for the lean-steer coupling.

carveRadiusSlow.unit: L, full steer at 0.54 sqrt(gL) (1.5 m/s real)
carveRadiusSlow.source: truck geometry (Hubbard 1979): wheelbase ~0.36 m, ~15 deg effective steer per truck at full lean gives R = WB / (2 tan d) ~ 0.67-0.8 m.

grindKeep.unit: speed kept after 3 L of flat rail, entered at 1.43 sqrt(gL)
grindKeep.source: Coulomb sliding of an aluminium truck on a steel rail, mu 0.25 +/- 0.1 (engineering tables: aluminium on steel 0.47 dry, waxed far lower): v^2 = 16 - 2 * 0.25 * 9.81 * 2.4 at 4 m/s real.

pipeDecay.unit: peak height ratio, wall to next wall, no input, from half wall height
pipeDecay.source: mu 0.02 (Kogelbauer et al.) over the ~4.7 m real path between walls of the game's own pipe scaled to L: dh 0.094 m on a 0.55 m peak.

pumpGain.unit: first-wall peak / start height (half the wall), pumping on the transitions only, capped at the coping
pumpGain.source: half-pipe amplitude law of Kogelbauer et al. (exponent 5 in r_max/r_min) with a 0.1-0.15 r centre-of-mass stroke; skilled riders go half height to coping in about 3 walls. Wide band.

vertAir.unit: best air above coping / wall height, held push, 15 s
vertAir.source: vert360flat and vert720: at the peak the board is roughly 1-1.5 m above a ~3.4 m vert coping (about 0.35 of the wall), judged against the rider's height (1.75 m); camera pans, so +/-0.15.
